comment: Performance baseline and budgets for scripts/check-performance.mjs.
All numbers are measured against the LOCAL generated docs/ site over a
loopback server (never the public internet), on a mobile viewport with
a fast-3G-class network profile and 4x CPU throttling — see the
'profile' block in the measurement output. Byte budgets are exact and
deterministic; timing budgets carry wide tolerances so CI never fails
on scheduler jitter. Run: npm run test:performance
The 'baseline' block is the measured state of the site BEFORE the 2026
performance work, kept for comparison; 'budgets' is what CI enforces.
budgetNotes: Budgets set 2026-07-17 from the post-optimisation measurements, with
headroom so CI fails on real regressions, not jitter: byte budgets sit
~10-15% above actual (CSS 28.5 KB, core JS 8.7 KB, total JS 20.2 KB,
largest HTML 126 KB, suggestions 161 KB, full index 662 KB); timing
budgets sit far above the observed values (script <= 31 ms, search
type-to-results 2420 ms on the throttled profile) because CPU-throttled
timings vary run to run. fontBytes is exactly 0 by design: the site
must not ship webfonts. maxInitialRequests covers the heaviest page
(search.html: html + css + core.js + search.js + worker + index +
fails the build if any non-search page downloads JSON during load.
